title: Research Question Generation
body:
Research Question Generation is a record in the Open-Ended Research Frontier Database. Proposed design for continuously proposing high-value research questions and measurable experiments. This record describes a proposed system design, not a claim that the capability already exists. It treats research question generation as a checkable unit of work: the inputs are stated plainly, the method is applied step by step, the result is recorded, and the checks are listed so that another reader can repeat the work and reach the same result. Every record in this database follows that same discipline, so the archive stays consistent as it grows.

Method. The working method for this record is Research question generation and assessment, applied within open-ended research. First, the question is written down in one sentence so its scope is clear. Second, the relevant inputs and assumptions are listed, including anything that is not yet known and any approximation limits that apply. Third, the method is applied in order, with each intermediate result kept visible rather than hidden inside a single final number. Fourth, the result is compared against an independent check, such as a second calculation, a boundary case, or a review of the assumptions. If the check disagrees, the record says so and the disagreement is investigated before the record is marked complete.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for research question generation. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand-typed claim. The demo reports candidates evaluated, checks passed, and verdict; readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this record when you need a documented, repeatable treatment of research question generation, when you want to show your working, or when a later reviewer must be able to audit what was assumed and what was concluded. Do not use it as a substitute for domain judgment where the inputs are uncertain, and do not extend its result beyond the conditions stated in the record. No capability is claimed beyond what the demo and the checks demonstrate. Public edition note. This record carries fact-checked public and methodology content for everyone.
